# Adjudication Task — Chapter 403

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃403화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|이십여 대의 군용 수송기와 호위를 위해 따라붙은 전투기들은 착륙부터 난항을 겪었다.
  6|
  7|「이, 이런.」
  8|
  9|「착륙 지점을 찾을 수 없습니다!」
 10|
 11|온통 폐허가 된 소도시.
 12|
 13|빼곡하게 들어찬 건축물들은 도미노처럼 쓰러져 있고, 곳곳에서는 화염이 솟구쳤다.
 14|
 15|하지만 무엇보다 파일럿들을 두렵게 만든 것은, 까마득한 상공에서도 내려다보이는 참혹한 광경이었다.
 16|
 17|학교 운동장, 편의점, 관공서…… 평화로운 일상이 사라진 그곳에는 시체의 산과 붉은 핏물의 강이 빈자리를 채우고 있었다.
 18|
 19|몬스터 군단이 그려 낸 한 폭의 지옥도(地獄道).
 20|
 21|생명이라고는 존재하지 않는 지상을 바라본 이들이 형용할 수 없는 공포에 몸을 떨던 그때였다.
 22|
 23|「착륙하게.」
 24|
 25|「초, 총사령관님. 하지만…….」
 26|
 27|「하지만이 아니라 반드시, 일세. 이건 명령이야.」
 28|
 29|묵직한 음성을 토해 낸 장년인의 굳은 얼굴을 마주한 파일럿은 선택의 여지가 없음을 깨달았다.
 30|
 31|자신은 군인이었고, 상대는 이번 전쟁을 지휘하는 실질적인 총사령관이었으니까.
 32|
 33|샤오 주석의 신임을 한몸에 받는 심복이자, 중앙 군사위원회 국방부장인 웨이펑후 상장의 명령에 불복하는 건 미친 짓이었다.
 34|
 35|그리고 다음 순간 이어진 웨이펑후의 한마디에, 파일럿은 생각했다.
 36|
 37|차라리 명령 불복종이 덜 미친 짓일 거라고.
 38|
 39|「서부 전선이 임시 본부로 삼은 종합병원으로 가게.」
 40|
 41|「예? 하지만 그곳은…….」
 42|
 43|「마지막으로 도착한 통신에 의하면 가장 치열한 격전이 벌어진 곳이겠지. 어쩌면 지금까지도. 나 역시 잘 알고 있네.」
 44|
 45|「…….」
 46|
 47|「어쩌면 이미 늦었을지도 모르네. 그러나 우린 가야 해. 아직 한 사람이라도 살아 있다면 그를 도와 싸워야지.」
 48|
 49|깊게 가라앉은 눈빛을 한 웨이펑후가 말을 이었다.
 50|
 51|「조종간을 잡게. 그리고 가장 먼저 착륙하게.」
 52|
 53|총사령관인 그가 직접 여기까지 온 것도 파격적인 일인데, 가장 먼저 착륙을 시도하라니. 아직 남아 있을 몬스터들을 생각하면 그야말로 엄청난 위험을 동반하는 일이다.
 54|
 55|‘빌어먹을.’
 56|
 57|눈을 질끈 감은 파일럿은 통신을 켰다. 이내 잘게 떨리는 목소리가 통신망을 타고 전 기체에 퍼져 나가기 시작했다.
 58|
 59|「VIP-777이 전 기체에 명령한다. 전 기체에 명령한다…….」
 60|
 61|자신의 명령이 하달되는 것을 들으며, 웨이펑후는 천천히 심호흡했다.
 62|
 63|만일의 사태를 대비해 몸에 걸친 낙하 장비가 천근 바위처럼 무겁게 느껴졌다.
 64|
 65|‘삼십여 년 만의 실전이라 그런가. 떨리는군.’
 66|
 67|그리고 이런 감정은 비단 웨이펑후 혼자만의 것이 아니었다.
 68|
 69|이십여 기의 군용 수송기에 몸을 실은 4천 명의 헌터 모두가 크고 작은 두려움을 품고 있었다.
 70|
 71|누군가는 당장이라도 도망치고 싶을 것이고, 누군가는 두려움을 억누르며 애써 전의를 불태우고 있을 것이다.
 72|
 73|곧 시작될 전투에서 누가 죽을지는 아무도 알 수 없다. 웨이펑후 역시 예외는 아니며, 총사령관인 그가 위험을 무릅쓰고 격전지에 온 것은 병사들의 사기 때문이었다.
 74|
 75|‘부하들만 사지로 몰아넣는다면 지휘관의 자격이 없다.’
 76|
 77|그것이 웨이펑후의 평생 지론이었고 친아들이나 다름없는 외조카, 레이페이는 그런 숙부를 존경했다.
 78|
 79|문득 눈앞을 스치는 그리운 얼굴에 늙은 장군의 가슴 한구석이 욱신거렸다.
 80|
 81|「……보고 싶구나.」
 82|
 83|웨이펑후는 작게 중얼거렸다.
 84|
 85|레이페이가 실종된 지 어느덧 보름. 하지만 그는 희망의 끈을 놓지 않았다. 안전한 곳으로 옮겨진 레이페이의 아내와 딸 역시 마찬가지였다.
 86|
 87|‘나는 오늘, 널 닮은 이를 보았다.’
 88|
 89|아직 이십 대에 불과한 젊은이. 머나먼 타지에서 엄청난 전공을 쌓은 그는 서부 전선이 위험에 빠졌다는 소식에 망설임 없이 떠났다.
 90|
 91|심지어 생존확률 10%에 불과한 텔레포트를 시도하며 웃었다고 했다.
 92|
 93|
 94|
 95|‘괜찮네요. 10% 정도면.’
 96|
 97|‘아마도, 차원을 넘을 확률보다는 천 배 정도 높을 테니까.’
 98|
 99|
100|
101|매직 존슨으로부터 그 소식을 전해 들었을 때, 웨이펑후는 즉시 총사령부의 전력을 동원해 편대를 꾸렸다.
102|
103|외국인에 불과한 청년, 진태경이 보여 준 기개에 충격을 받았고 그런 그의 모습에서 실종된 외조카를 떠올렸다.
104|
105|‘너 역시 그리했겠지. 그렇지 않으냐?’
106|
107|들리지 않는 물음을 던진 웨이펑후의 입가에 희미한 미소가 맺힌 바로 그 순간이었다.
108|
109|「이, 이럴 수가……!」
110|
111|「초, 총사령관님!」
112|
113|파일럿들의 다급한 외침에 고개를 내민 웨이펑후의 시선이 창밖을 향했다.
114|
115|서서히 가까워지는 지상, 그곳에는 지금껏 목격한 어느 전장보다 참혹한 시산혈해(屍山血海)가 펼쳐져 있었다.
116|
117|시체와 피, 피와 시체…….
118|
119|서부 전선의 임시 사령부인 종합병원은 처참히 무너져 흉한 철골을 드러냈고, 지옥의 입구처럼 뻥 뚫린 거대한 싱크홀(Sinkhole)과 지면에 아로새겨진 수십 개의 크레이터에는 적녹색의 핏물이 가득 채워져 있었다.
120|
121|뒤섞여 쓰러진 몬스터와 인간의 시체는 헤아릴 수도 없이 많았다. 수천? 아니, 일만을 훌쩍 넘겼다.
122|
123|「……맙소사.」
124|
125|「도, 도대체 누가?」
126|
127|재앙이 할퀴고 지나간 죽음의 땅.
128|
129|할 말을 잃고 처참한 지상을 바라보던 파일럿들은 웨이펑후의 외침에 퍼뜩 정신을 차렸다.
130|
131|「고도를 낮추게, 어서!」
132|
133|「예, 옛!」
134|
135|몬스터에 대한 위협은 사라졌지만 방심해서는 안 된다.
136|
137|파일럿은 어느 때보다 신중하게 기체를 조종했고, 식은땀으로 몸이 흠뻑 젖은 상태로 착륙을 시도했다.
138|
139|키기기기긱, 쿠쿵!
140|
141|수차례의 격한 진동이 휩쓸고 지나간 기체. 마침내 착륙에 성공한 수송기에서 가장 먼저 내린 사람은 다름 아닌 웨이펑후였다.
142|
143|타다다닥!
144|
145|그의 뒤를 따라 수송기에 탑승해 있던 이백여 명의 헌터들이 신속히 지상에 발을 디뎠다.
146|
147|그리고 그들이 보인 반응은 두 가지로 나뉘었다.
148|
149|「이런 미친…….」
150|
151|상상치도 못한 광경에 대한 경악.
152|
153|「우욱, 우웨에에엑!」
154|
155|주위를 가득 메운 피비린내와 조각난 시신들로부터 느끼는 욕지기.
156|
157|동시에 뇌리를 가득 채운 의문.
158|
159|‘도대체 누가?’
160|
161|생존자를 찾아야 한다는 것도 잊은 채, 웨이펑후를 비롯한 모든 이들이 석상처럼 굳어 버린 바로 그 순간이었다.
162|
163|철벅, 철벅.
164|
165|고요한 전장에 울려 퍼지는 발걸음 소리.
166|
167|바닥에 고인 핏물을 밟으며 전장을 가로지르는 한 사람을 향해 이백여 쌍의 시선이 몰려들었다.
168|
169|머리부터 발끝까지, 온통 녹색 피를 뒤집어쓴 그를 바라보던 웨이펑후가 신음처럼 중얼거렸다.
170|
171|「진 선생……?」
172|
173|분명 그였다.
174|
175|혈인(血人)이나 다름없는 모습이었지만 웨이펑후는 알아볼 수 있었다.
176|
177|생존확률 10%의 텔레포트 마법, 암담한 전황을 뒤집고 진태경은 살아남았다.
178|
179|멈추지 않을 것 같던 그의 걸음이 웨이펑후의 앞에서 정지했다.
180|
181|철벅.
182|
183|몬스터의 끈적한 핏물로 엉겨 붙은 머리카락을 쓸어올린 진태경은, 침묵 끝에 첫 마디를 뗐다.
184|
185|“전투는 끝났습니다. 살아남은 몬스터는…… 없습니다.”
186|
187|「……!」
188|
189|「……!」
190|
191|믿을 수 없는 그의 한마디에, 좌중은 전율에 휩싸였다.
192|
193|서부 전선에서 보내온 마지막 통신에 의하면 몬스터 군단의 숫자는 자그마치 일만에 달했다.
194|
195|그뿐만이 아니다. 아크 리치의 심복으로 여겨지는 데스나이트 로드가 직접 나섰으니 다섯 개 전선 중 가장 압도적인 공세였다.
196|
197|반면 그에 맞서 싸운 헌터의 숫자는 고작 천여 명. 그 외의 인민해방군은 종잇조각이나 다름없었다.
198|
199|‘그런 전투에서 이긴 것으로도 모자라, 일만의 몬스터 군단을 전멸시키다니.’
200|
201|한 사람이 없었다면 불가능했을 전투. 동시에 한 사람이 있었기에 가능했던 승리.
202|
203|S급 헌터가 단번에 전황을 뒤집을 수 있는 전략 병기라지만, 대격변 이래 그 누가 이런 업적을 세웠던가.
204|
205|이백여 명의 헌터는 경외(敬畏) 어린 시선으로 눈앞의 청년을 바라보았다.
206|
207|그러나 한 사람, 웨이펑후만큼은 달랐다.
208|
209|늙은 장군은 슬픔과 두려움이 담긴 눈빛으로 진태경을 응시했다. 아니, 그의 손에 들린 한 자루 검을 바라보고 있었다.
210|
211|더 없이 눈에 익은 검이었고, 그래서 더 가슴이 아팠다.
212|
213|지금의 상황이 무엇을 뜻하는지 알기에.
214|
215|「그 아이를…… 만났소?」
216|
217|잠시 침묵하던 진태경이 대답했다.
218|
219|“사랑한다고 전해 달라더군요.”
220|
221|「……!」
222|
223|“미안하다고도 했습니다.”
224|
225|웨이펑후는 새어 나오는 울음을 참으려 이를 악물었다. 희뿌옇게 물드는 시야 속에서, 마지막 한마디가 귓가에 닿았다.
226|
227|“제가 본 최고의 헌터였습니다.”
228|
229|거기까지였다. 투툭, 웨이펑후의 주름진 피부 위로 눈물이 흘러내렸다.
230|
231|어디선가 불어온 바람이 그를 부드럽게 감싸 안았다.
232|
233|
234|
235|* * *
236|
237|
238|
239|등급이나 업적, 헌터냐 아니냐는 중요하지 않다.
240|
241|다른 사람의 위해 스스로를 희생했다는 것만으로도 그는 영웅이라 불릴 자격이 충분하니까.
242|
243|그렇기에 레이페이는 내 기억에 오래도록 남아 있을 것이다.
244|
245|언데드로 부활했으나 인간으로 죽은 자.
246|
247|마지막까지 사명을 다한 그야말로 진정한 헌터고, 영웅이다.
248|
249|오늘 이 자리에서 죽어 간 수많은 이들 역시 마찬가지였다.
250|
251|그리고…… 아직 의식을 회복하지 못한 두 사람도.
252|
253|‘피로가 모두 회복되기 전까지는 깨어나지 않을 거라고 했었지.’
254|
255|앞서 다녀간 힐러가 해 준 말을 떠올리며, 깊은 잠에 빠진 최 팀장과 샤오 쉔을 바라봤다.
256|
257|최상급 포션 덕분에 두 사람의 부상은 씻은 듯이 나았지만, 신체와 정신에 누적된 피로는 별개의 문제다.
258|
259|‘레벨 업을 하는 나조차도 가끔은 기절하니까.’
260|
261|두 사람은 마지막까지 용감하게 싸웠다.
262|
263|사지가 잘려 나가는 고통 속에서도 손에 쥔 무기를 놓지 않을 만큼.
264|
265|“영웅, 영웅이라…….”
266|
267|낮게 뇌까린 나는 옆에 놓아둔 검을 바라보았다. 바로 그 영웅이 남긴 검이자 유품.
268|
269|하염없이 눈물을 흘리던 웨이펑후는 극구 사양하는 내게 그 검을 돌려주며 말했다.
270|
271|
272|
273|‘그 녀석도 진 선생이 맡아 주길 원했을 거요.’
274|
275|
276|
277|정말입니까, 레이페이?
278|
279|답이 돌아오지 않을 질문을 던지며 검신을 매만졌다. 보는 것만으로도 서늘한 예기(銳氣)가 느껴지는 명검이다.
280|
281|‘아이템 감정.’
282|
283|띠링.

- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

By contrast, barely a thousand Hunters had stood against them. The remaining People’s Liberation Army troops might as well have been made of paper.

[P99]
*Not only did they win—they wiped out an army of ten thousand monsters.*

[P100]
It was a battle that would have been impossible without one man.

[P101]
And a victory made possible because that one man had been there.

[P102]
An S-rank Hunter was said to be a strategic weapon capable of overturning an entire battlefield in an instant. But since the Great Cataclysm, who had ever accomplished something like this?

[P103]
The two hundred Hunters gazed at the young man before them in awe.

[P104]
But Wei Fenghu was different.

[P105]
The old general stared at Jin Taekyung with grief and fear in his eyes.

[P106]
No—not at Jin Taekyung himself.

[P107]
At the sword in his hand.

[P108]
Wei Fenghu knew that sword all too well, which only made the pain in his heart worse.

[P109]
He knew what its presence meant.

[P110]
“Did you… meet him?”

[P111]
After a brief silence, Jin Taekyung answered.

[P112]
“He asked me to tell them he loved them.”

[P113]
“…!”

[P114]
“He also said he was sorry.”

[P115]
Wei Fenghu clenched his teeth against the sob rising in his throat. Through his tear-clouded vision, he heard one final sentence.

[P116]
“He was the best Hunter I’ve ever seen.”

[P117]
That was all.

[P118]
Tears rolled down Wei Fenghu’s wrinkled face.

[P119]
A breeze blew from somewhere and gently wrapped around him.

[P120]
* * *

[P121]
Rank, achievements, whether someone was a Hunter or not—none of it mattered.

[P122]
The fact that he had sacrificed himself for others was more than enough to call him a hero.

[P123]
That was why Lei Fei would remain in my memory for a long time.

[P124]
A man resurrected as an undead who died as a human.

[P125]
He had fulfilled his mission to the very end. He was a true Hunter and a true hero.

[P126]
The countless others who had died here today were no different.

[P127]
And neither were the two people who had yet to regain consciousness.

[P128]
*The healer said they wouldn’t wake up until they’d recovered from their exhaustion.*

[P129]
Remembering what the healer who had stopped by earlier had told me, I looked at Team Leader Choi and Shao Shen, both sunk in a deep sleep.

[P130]
Thanks to the top-grade potion, their injuries had vanished as if they had never existed. But the fatigue accumulated in their bodies and minds was a separate matter.

[P131]
*Even I pass out sometimes, and I can level up.*

[P132]
The two of them had fought bravely to the very end.

[P133]
Even through the agony of having their limbs torn off, they had refused to let go of their weapons.

[P134]
“Heroes… heroes, huh.”

[P135]
I muttered under my breath and looked at the sword lying beside me.

[P136]
The sword left behind by that very hero. His keepsake.

[P137]
Wei Fenghu had wept without end as he returned it to me despite my repeated refusal.

[P138]
*“He would have wanted you to keep it too, Mr. Jin.”*

[P139]
*Really, Lei Fei?*

[P140]
I ran my fingers over the blade as I asked a question that would never receive an answer.

[P141]
It was a magnificent sword, its chilling edge apparent at a glance.

[P142]
*Item appraisal.*

[P143]
Ding.

[P144]
> **System**
>
> **Item Window**
>
> **Hero’s Soul**
>
> **Type:** Sword  
> **Grade:** Supreme Peak  
> **Restriction:** Those worthy of being called heroes  
> **Description:** Extremely hard and sharp. The final spirit of a noble hero dwells within it, and those who meet its qualifications can draw out even greater power.

[P145]
*Hero’s Soul?*

[P146]
It was a fitting name for something that had belonged to Lei Fei, but this was certainly an unusual sword.

[P147]
Its Supreme Peak Grade made sense, considering it had survived that fierce battle without so much as a hairline crack. The restriction, however, was unique.

[P148]
*Only someone with an upright character can use it?*

[P149]
Hmm. Might as well put it to the test.

[P150]
Without hesitation, I gripped the hilt and slashed downward through the air.

[P151]
Whoosh!

[P152]
Better than I expected.

[P153]
The weight and balance were perfect, and I liked how its edge seemed sharp enough to split the wind itself. The System notification that immediately followed was the icing on the cake.

[P154]
Ding.

[P155]
> **System**
>
> - **Hero’s Soul** has recognized you as someone of upright character.
> - **Hero’s Power** has manifested. All stats have increased slightly, and fatigue has been reduced. You may draw out even greater power under certain circumstances.

[P156]
I had no idea what those certain circumstances were, but apparently this wasn’t one of them. The increase in my stats was so tiny I couldn’t feel it at all.

[P157]
It was like adding a single bucket of water to a lake.

[P158]
*Still, it would be perfect for judging someone’s character.*

[P159]
A character-testing sword.

[P160]
From now on, I would test everyone who approached me with Hero’s Soul. If the sword accepted them, I’d keep them close. If it didn’t, I’d cut them down, root and branch—snip…

[P161]
Crackle!

[P162]
A powerful electric current suddenly shot through my hand, and I dropped the sword.

[P163]
“What the hell?”

[P164]
As bewilderment washed over me, a sharp alarm sounded and a System message appeared in the air.

[P165]
Beep!

[P166]
> **System**
>
> - You have harbored an evil intention!
> - **Hero’s Soul** has rejected you!
> - The effect of **Hero’s Power** has disappeared!

[P167]
“…”

[P168]
Come on. It was just a passing thought.

[P169]
I looked down at the fallen sword and let out a short laugh. It suddenly occurred to me that perhaps a little of Lei Fei’s soul really did linger within it.

[P170]
Wait. If that was true…

[P171]
“Are you listening?”

[P172]
After a brief silence, the Skeleton Warlord, currently stored inside my inventory, answered.

[P173]
—…I am.

[P174]
“I wanted to ask you something.”

[P175]
—…If your question concerns whether that sword is an Ego Sword, the answer is no. Only the faintest trace of a soul remains within it. The human you are thinking of has already ceased to exist.

[P176]
He usually had a screw loose, but he was still a named monster and the commander of an army of the dead.

[P177]
He had absorbed some of the mana scattered during Lei Fei’s Erasure and grown even stronger, so there was a good chance he was right.

[P178]
That aside…

[P179]
“Is something wrong?”

[P180]
—Hmm?

[P181]
“You’ve seemed gloomy for a while.”

[P182]
Even as I said it, I wondered if the question made any sense. Why was I asking an undead monster why he seemed gloomy? Weren’t they gloomy by nature?

[P183]
*The problem is, he doesn’t usually act like this.*

[P184]
Then the Skeleton Warlord suddenly spoke.

[P185]
—A thought occurred to me.

[P186]
“What thought?”

[P187]
—What kind of being was I in the past?

[P188]
“…!”

[P189]
—I have no memories at all. Although the human named Lei Fei has ceased to exist, this commander envied him. At least he learned who he was.

[P190]
I hadn’t expected him to be thinking about something like that.

[P191]
After considering it for a moment, I spoke in a warm voice.

[P192]
“Then should I erase you too?”

[P193]
—…!

[P194]
“What? You said you were envious.”

[P195]
—N-No, that isn’t what I meant…

[P196]
The Skeleton Warlord’s frantic explanation was cut short by a knock and a polite voice from beyond the door.

[P197]
“Mr. Jin. Comrade Minister of State would like to see you.”

[P198]
It seemed it was already time.

[P199]
“Yes. I’ll be right there.”

[P200]
I took one last look at the two sleeping figures, then rose from my seat. As I did, I murmured the words I hadn’t managed to say earlier.

[P201]
“Well, if you ask me, you were probably a pretty decent guy.”

[P202]
—…Huh? Were you talking to this commander?

[P203]
“No. Just talking to myself.”

[P204]
—Ahem. Of course.

[P205]
But the sudden brightness in the Skeleton Warlord’s previously dejected voice was definitely not my imagination.

[P206]
I let out a quiet laugh and left the room.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Wei Fenghu continued, his eyes grave.

[P24]
“Take us down. And be the first to land.”

[P25]
It was extraordinary enough that the commander-in-chief had come all the way here himself. Now he was ordering his plane to land first. With monsters potentially still in the area, the risk was enormous.

[P26]
*Damn it.*

[P27]
The pilot squeezed his eyes shut and switched on the radio. His trembling voice soon spread across the communications network to every aircraft.

[P28]
“VIP-777 to all aircraft. I repeat, VIP-777 to all aircraft…”

[P29]
As he listened to his orders being relayed, Wei Fenghu slowly drew a deep breath.

[P30]
The parachute strapped to his body in case of an emergency felt as heavy as a massive boulder.

[P31]
*Is it because this is my first real battle in more than thirty years? I’m trembling.*

[P32]
And Wei Fenghu was not the only one.

[P33]
All four thousand Hunters aboard the twenty-odd military transports carried fears of their own.

[P34]
Some probably wanted to run away that very instant. Others were suppressing their fear and desperately trying to stoke their will to fight.

[P35]
No one knew who would die in the battle about to begin. Wei Fenghu was no exception. The reason he had risked coming to the fiercest part of the battlefield despite being the commander-in-chief was simple: the morale of his soldiers.

[P36]
*A commander who sends only his subordinates to their deaths has no right to command.*

[P37]
That had been Wei Fenghu’s lifelong principle, and Lei Fei—his nephew and as good as a son to him—had respected him for it.

[P38]
The sudden memory of that beloved face sent an ache through the old general’s heart.

[P39]
“…I miss you.”

[P40]
Wei Fenghu murmured quietly.

[P41]
It had already been fifteen days since Lei Fei disappeared. But he had not given up hope. Neither had Lei Fei’s wife and daughter, who had been moved somewhere safe.

[P42]
*Today, I saw someone who reminded me of you.*

[P43]
A young man still only in his twenties. He had accomplished incredible feats in a distant foreign land, and when he heard that the Western Front was in danger, he had left without a moment’s hesitation.

[P44]
He had even laughed before attempting a Teleport with only a ten-percent chance of survival.

[P45]
*“Ten percent sounds pretty good.”*

[P46]
*“It’s probably a thousand times higher than the odds of crossing dimensions.”*

[P47]
When Magic Johnson relayed those words, Wei Fenghu had immediately mobilized the command headquarters’ forces and assembled the squadron.

[P48]
He had been deeply moved by the courage shown by Jin Taekyung, a young foreigner, and the sight of him had brought his missing nephew to mind.

[P49]
*You would have done the same, wouldn’t you?*

[P50]
A faint smile had just touched Wei Fenghu’s lips when the pilots cried out.

[P51]
“H-How can this be…?”

[P52]
“C-Commander-in-Chief!”

[P53]
Wei Fenghu raised his head at their urgent shouts and looked out the window.

[P54]
As the ground drew closer, a sea of corpses and blood came into view, more horrific than any battlefield he had ever witnessed.

[P55]
Corpses and blood. Blood and corpses…

[P56]
The general hospital serving as the Western Front’s temporary headquarters lay in ruins, its twisted steel framework exposed. A gigantic sinkhole gaped like the entrance to hell, and dozens of craters carved into the ground brimmed with red and green blood.

[P57]
Monster and human corpses lay tangled together in numbers too vast to count.

[P58]
Thousands?

[P59]
No. Well over ten thousand.

[P60]
“My God…”

[P61]
“W-Who did this?”

[P62]
A land of death raked by disaster.

[P63]
The pilots stared speechlessly at the devastated ground until Wei Fenghu’s shout jolted them back to their senses.

[P64]
“Lower our altitude! Quickly!”

[P65]
“Yes, sir!”

[P66]
The threat from the monsters appeared to be gone, but they could not afford to let their guard down.

[P67]
The pilot maneuvered the aircraft more carefully than ever, his entire body drenched in cold sweat as he attempted the landing.

[P68]
Krrrrrrk, boom!

[P69]
The aircraft shuddered violently several times. When the transport finally came to a stop, the first person out was none other than Wei Fenghu.

[P70]
Tat-tat-tat!

[P71]
The two hundred Hunters aboard the transport quickly poured out behind him.

[P72]
Their reactions fell into two categories.

[P73]
“This is fucking insane…”

[P74]
Shock at a sight beyond anything they had imagined.

[P75]
“Urk… Urrrgh!”

[P76]
Nausea from the stench of blood filling the air and the dismembered corpses strewn everywhere.

[P77]
And through it all, one question filled every mind.

[P78]
*Who did this?*

[P79]
They had even forgotten they were supposed to search for survivors. Wei Fenghu and everyone else stood frozen like statues.

[P80]
Then—

[P81]
Splash. Splash.

[P82]
Footsteps echoed across the silent battlefield.

[P83]
Two hundred pairs of eyes turned toward a lone figure crossing the field, wading through pools of blood.

[P84]
The man was drenched in green blood from head to toe. Wei Fenghu stared at him and groaned out a name.

[P85]
“Mr. Jin…?”

[P86]
It was him.

[P87]
Though he looked like a man made of blood, Wei Fenghu recognized him.

[P88]
Jin Taekyung had survived a Teleport spell with only a ten-percent survival rate, overturned a hopeless battle, and lived.

[P89]
His seemingly endless steps finally came to a halt before Wei Fenghu.

[P90]
Splash.

[P91]
Jin Taekyung pushed back the hair clotted with sticky monster blood. After a long silence, he spoke.

[P92]
“The battle is over. There are… no monsters left alive.”

[P93]
“…!”

[P94]
“…!”

[P95]
That unbelievable declaration sent a shudder through everyone present.

[P96]
According to the Western Front’s final transmission, the monster army had numbered a staggering ten thousand.

[P97]
And that was not all. A Death Knight Lord believed to be one of the Arch Lich’s closest servants had personally entered the battle, making this the most overwhelming offensive of the five fronts.

[P98]
By contrast, barely a thousand Hunters had stood against them. The remaining People’s Liberation Army troops might as well have been made of paper.

[P99]
*Not only did they win—they wiped out an army of ten thousand monsters.*

[P100]
It was a battle that would have been impossible without one man.

[P101]
And a victory made possible because that one man had been there.

[P102]
An S-rank Hunter was said to be a strategic weapon capable of overturning an entire battlefield in an instant. But since the Great Cataclysm, who had ever accomplished something like this?

[P103]
The two hundred Hunters gazed at the young man before them in awe.

[P104]
But Wei Fenghu was different.

[P105]
The old general stared at Jin Taekyung with grief and fear in his eyes.

[P106]
No—not at Jin Taekyung himself.

[P107]
At the sword in his hand.

[P108]
Wei Fenghu knew that sword all too well, which only made the pain in his heart worse.

[P109]
He knew what its presence meant.

[P110]
“Did you… meet him?”

[P111]
After a brief silence, Jin Taekyung answered.

[P112]
“He asked me to tell them he loved them.”

[P113]
“…!”

[P114]
“He also said he was sorry.”

[P115]
Wei Fenghu clenched his teeth against the sob rising in his throat. Through his tear-clouded vision, he heard one final sentence.

[P116]
“He was the best Hunter I’ve ever seen.”

[P117]
That was all.

[P118]
Tears rolled down Wei Fenghu’s wrinkled face.

[P119]
A breeze blew from somewhere and gently wrapped around him.

[P120]
* * *

[P121]
Rank, achievements, whether someone was a Hunter or not—none of it mattered.

[P122]
The fact that he had sacrificed himself for others was more than enough to call him a hero.

[P123]
That was why Lei Fei would remain in my memory for a long time.

[P124]
A man resurrected as an undead who died as a human.

[P125]
He had fulfilled his mission to the very end. He was a true Hunter and a true hero.

[P126]
The countless others who had died here today were no different.

[P127]
And neither were the two people who had yet to regain consciousness.

[P128]
*The healer said they wouldn’t wake up until they’d recovered from their exhaustion.*

[P129]
Remembering what the healer who had stopped by earlier had told me, I looked at Team Leader Choi and Shao Shen, both sunk in a deep sleep.

[P130]
Thanks to the top-grade potion, their injuries had vanished as if they had never existed. But the fatigue accumulated in their bodies and minds was a separate matter.

[P131]
*Even I pass out sometimes, and I can level up.*

[P132]
The two of them had fought bravely to the very end.

[P133]
Even through the agony of having their limbs torn off, they had refused to let go of their weapons.

[P134]
“Heroes… heroes, huh.”

[P135]
I muttered under my breath and looked at the sword lying beside me.

[P136]
The sword left behind by that very hero. His keepsake.

[P137]
Wei Fenghu had wept without end as he returned it to me despite my repeated refusal.

[P138]
*“He would have wanted you to keep it too, Mr. Jin.”*

[P139]
*Really, Lei Fei?*

[P140]
I ran my fingers over the blade as I asked a question that would never receive an answer.

[P141]
It was a magnificent sword, its chilling edge apparent at a glance.

[P142]
*Item appraisal.*

[P143]
Ding.

[P144]
> **System**
>
> **Item Window**
>
> **Hero’s Soul**
>
> **Type:** Sword  
> **Grade:** Supreme Peak  
> **Restriction:** Those worthy of being called heroes  
> **Description:** Extremely hard and sharp. The final spirit of a noble hero dwells within it, and those who meet its qualifications can draw out even greater power.

[P145]
*Hero’s Soul?*

[P146]
It was a fitting name for something that had belonged to Lei Fei, but this was certainly an unusual sword.

[P147]
Its Supreme Peak Grade made sense, considering it had survived that fierce battle without so much as a hairline crack. The restriction, however, was unique.

[P148]
*Only someone with an upright character can use it?*

[P149]
Hmm. Might as well put it to the test.

[P150]
Without hesitation, I gripped the hilt and slashed downward through the air.

[P151]
Whoosh!

[P152]
Better than I expected.

[P153]
The weight and balance were perfect, and I liked how its edge seemed sharp enough to split the wind itself. The System notification that immediately followed was the icing on the cake.

[P154]
Ding.

[P155]
> **System**
>
> - **Hero’s Soul** has recognized you as someone of upright character.
> - **Hero’s Power** has manifested. All stats have increased slightly, and fatigue has been reduced. You may draw out even greater power under certain circumstances.

[P156]
I had no idea what those certain circumstances were, but apparently this wasn’t one of them. The increase in my stats was so tiny I couldn’t feel it at all.

[P157]
It was like adding a single bucket of water to a lake.

[P158]
*Still, it would be perfect for judging someone’s character.*

[P159]
A character-testing sword.

[P160]
From now on, I would test everyone who approached me with Hero’s Soul. If the sword accepted them, I’d keep them close. If it didn’t, I’d cut them down, root and branch—snip…

[P161]
Crackle!

[P162]
A powerful electric current suddenly shot through my hand, and I dropped the sword.

[P163]
“What the hell?”

[P164]
As bewilderment washed over me, a sharp alarm sounded and a System message appeared in the air.

[P165]
Beep!

[P166]
> **System**
>
> - You have harbored an evil intention!
> - **Hero’s Soul** has rejected you!
> - The effect of **Hero’s Power** has disappeared!

[P167]
“…”

[P168]
Come on. It was just a passing thought.

[P169]
I looked down at the fallen sword and let out a short laugh. It suddenly occurred to me that perhaps a little of Lei Fei’s soul really did linger within it.

[P170]
Wait. If that was true…

[P171]
“Are you listening?”

[P172]
After a brief silence, the Skeleton Warlord, currently stored inside my inventory, answered.

[P173]
—…I am.

[P174]
“I wanted to ask you something.”

[P175]
—…If your question concerns whether that sword is an Ego Sword, the answer is no. Only the faintest trace of a soul remains within it. The human you are thinking of has already ceased to exist.

[P176]
He usually had a screw loose, but he was still a named monster and the commander of an army of the dead.

[P177]
He had absorbed some of the mana scattered during Lei Fei’s Erasure and grown even stronger, so there was a good chance he was right.

[P178]
That aside…

[P179]
“Is something wrong?”

[P180]
—Hmm?

[P181]
“You’ve seemed gloomy for a while.”

[P182]
Even as I said it, I wondered if the question made any sense. Why was I asking an undead monster why he seemed gloomy? Weren’t they gloomy by nature?

[P183]
*The problem is, he doesn’t usually act like this.*

[P184]
Then the Skeleton Warlord suddenly spoke.

[P185]
—A thought occurred to me.

[P186]
“What thought?”

[P187]
—What kind of being was I in the past?

[P188]
“…!”

[P189]
—I have no memories at all. Although the human named Lei Fei has ceased to exist, this commander envied him. At least he learned who he was.

[P190]
I hadn’t expected him to be thinking about something like that.

[P191]
After considering it for a moment, I spoke in a warm voice.

[P192]
“Then should I erase you too?”

[P193]
—…!

[P194]
“What? You said you were envious.”

[P195]
—N-No, that isn’t what I meant…

[P196]
The Skeleton Warlord’s frantic explanation was cut short by a knock and a polite voice from beyond the door.

[P197]
“Mr. Jin. Comrade Minister of State would like to see you.”

[P198]
It seemed it was already time.

[P199]
“Yes. I’ll be right there.”

[P200]
I took one last look at the two sleeping figures, then rose from my seat. As I did, I murmured the words I hadn’t managed to say earlier.

[P201]
“Well, if you ask me, you were probably a pretty decent guy.”

[P202]
—…Huh? Were you talking to this commander?

[P203]
“No. Just talking to myself.”

[P204]
—Ahem. Of course.

[P205]
But the sudden brightness in the Skeleton Warlord’s previously dejected voice was definitely not my imagination.

[P206]
I let out a quiet laugh and left the room.
